builder_plan.change: Change only the attention cache policy, after checking model and runtime support.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model with its ordinary attention cache.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak cache memory, long-context answer quality, first-token latency, and requests completed.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Storing the Gemma 4 K=V Cache Once: Exact Global-KV Memory Savings in a Paged Serving Engine with Unchanged Attention Kernels
summary: The method replaces storing a full key and full value for each global-attention KV head/token with one 640-value row exposed to unchanged paged attention as two overlapping strided key/value views. It costs engine integration and verification effort, makes eager decode steps 4% to 9% slower at equal batch, and does not yet compose with the default 8-bit KV-cache scale. It can fail when the served model lacks Gemma 4's exact normalized-key/value relationship and partial RoPE layout, when attention/paging/block-pool or transfer paths differ from the prototype, or when numerical-cache settings change enough to lose bit-level equivalence.
rationale: It is an exact KV-storage reduction with meaningful memory and decode-throughput gains, but it depends on Gemma 4's specific K/V parameterization and a prototype serving stack, so it should be validated only on the intended model and engine.

claims.statement: The method replaces storing a full key and full value for each global-attention KV head/token with one 640-value row exposed to unchanged paged attention as two overlapping strided key/value views. It costs engine integration and verification effort, makes eager decode steps 4% to 9% slower at equal batch, and does not yet compose with the default 8-bit KV-cache scale. It can fail when the served model lacks Gemma 4's exact normalized-key/value relationship and partial RoPE layout, when attention/paging/block-pool or transfer paths differ from the prototype, or when numerical-cache settings change enough to lose bit-level equivalence.

Steady decode KV memory per request falls by a factor of 1.34 to 1.40 at 32K to 64K tokens; decode tokens per step rise 1.38x for 16K-token prompts and 1.24x for 8K-token prompts in the reported two-A100 setup.
